feed.headline: Shock of rail tragedy gives way to sorrow and outrage in politically divided Spain
feed.ai: The latest train crash will pile pressure on the government of Pedro Sánchez, one month before the general election.

feed.headline: Spain train disaster clouds Sánchez chances of re-election
feed.ai: The Spanish PM is hit by a succession of crises just weeks before a snap general election.

feed.headline: Student-backed election winners demand sweeping resignations in Serbia
feed.ai: Days after ousting Aleksandar Vučić's party from power, Student List MPs call for top figures to stand down.

feed.headline: Post Office suspends sending goods to the EU
feed.ai: It follows a delay in updates to processing systems to allow for changes to EU customs rules.

feed.headline: EU chief lays out vision for new Canada partnership at Montreal summit
feed.ai: Ursula von der Leyen continued to use the term "associate member" for Canada despite some opposition of the bloc's members, including Germany.

feed.headline: Joy and disbelief on Serbian streets as Vučić concedes election defeat
feed.ai: BBC correspondent Nick Thorpe reports from Belgrade, where there were rapturous celebrations following the victory of the student-led movement.

feed.headline: Who actually controls Ukraine's access to Starlink?
feed.ai: President Zelensky says limits to the technology continue to affect Ukrainian forces, while US officials and Elon Musk offer conflicting accounts of who controls it.

feed.headline: French officials eye social media’s role in promoting unrest.
feed.ai: President Emmanuel Macron denied that the government had considered suspending online platforms, but he said they would have to be “vigilant” about preventing misuse.

feed.headline: Train Disaster Is a Blow to Spain’s Leader, Already an Election Underdog
feed.ai: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez wanted to campaign on inequality and housing, but the second major rail accident this year has put his government’s competence on trial.

feed.headline: Wanted: New Central Bank Chief. Expertise and Political Acumen Required.
feed.ai: The looming departure of the European Central Bank’s president, Christine Lagarde, has set in motion a high-stakes search for her successor.

feed.headline: Britain’s Prime Minister Says He’s Open to a Formal Apology for Slavery
feed.ai: The premier’s comments represent a major change in British policy, but they are unlikely to satisfy those who hoped that reparations would follow.

feed.headline: Kärcher boss: Less regulation, more action to get Europe and Germany fit again
feed.ai: Kärcher, best known for its pressure washers, recorded €3.5 billion in sales in 2025 and employs 17,000 people worldwide. Its CEO warns of a 'perfect storm' and calls for a fitness plan for Germany and Europe.
